canonical_question: Does the in situ annealing at 1123 K before irradiation serve to relax the as-deposited film, and could this temperature be close to the phase decomposition temperature observed in the CE simulations?

question_variants.question: Does the in situ annealing at 1123 K before irradiation serve to relax the as-deposited film, and could this temperature be close to the phase decomposition temperature observed in the CE simulations?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The paper mentions in situ annealing at 1123 K before irradiation but does not explicitly state the justification (e.g., relaxation) or compare this temperature to phase decomposition temperatures from CE simulations.

answers.answer: The text states samples were annealed in situ at 1123 K, but does not explicitly link this to stress relaxation or compare it to CE-simulated decomposition temperatures.
answers.conditions: in situ TEM, Gatan heating holder
answers.boundary_limitation: No explicit connection made between annealing temperature and CE simulation results.
evidence_spans: A detailed characterization of the morphology and phase details of the as-deposited HEA films results in a bimodal grain size distribution with ~70% of the grains with size in the nanocrystalline regime (≤100 nm) and some regions of ultrafine grain sizes (100 to 500 nm) with an underlying single-phase BCC, with a lattice constant of ~3.2 Å
APT confirmed the EDS results, showing a film composition of 38% (±0.09) W, 36% (±0.09) Ta, 15% (±0.05) Cr, and 11% (±0.05) V.
The morphology is composed of very distinct compositional striations (layering) within the grains of ~4-nm thickness, which was not observed in EDS.

source_evidence_spans: the samples were annealed in situ inside the TEM with a Gatan heating holder at 1123 K
